sources.entry: Calyx - Native macOS terminal for running and supervising coding agents in parallel. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/yuuichieguchi/Calyx) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Calyx is a native macOS terminal app, built on libghostty, for running and supervising multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Grok, pi) in parallel.
summary.what_it_does: Calyx provides a terminal workspace with tabs, split panes, and tab groups, and shows every connected coding agent's state (working, blocked, idle, done) in an Agents Sidebar with unread badges and click-to-focus. An opt-in Approval Inbox queues permission prompts from Claude Code, Codex, always-approve Grok sessions, and pi tool calls into one panel, and it can answer AskUserQuestion prompts. A Git sidebar shows working changes, commit graph, and diffs, where line-level review comments can be submitted to an agent pane. Calyx exposes panes, command logs, browser tabs, language servers (LSP), and peer messaging to agents through a built-in MCP server and bundled CLI, and it offers persistent daemon-backed sessions, remote sessions over SSH, and a Mission Map overview of all panes. Worktree Tasks create a branch and linked worktree for an agent, and an optional Usage Tracking feature records Claude Code token counts locally.
use_cases: run several coding agents in parallel without watching every terminal
approve or deny agent tool calls from one place
review agent-made diffs and send line comments back to the agent
let coding agents message each other across terminal panes
keep terminal sessions alive across app quit or crashes
start an agent on a new git branch in its own worktree
track Claude Code token usage per project locally
how_to_run: Download Calyx.zip from the latest release and move Calyx.app to /Applications
notable: Approval Inbox: opt-in, notification-style panel for permission prompts across all panes, with an Options pull-down and nothing auto-approved unless opted in
Mission Map (Cmd+Shift+M) lays out all panes as cards showing agent state, branch, current tool, and pending approvals
Built-in MCP server (AI Agent IPC) lets agents discover peers, send messages, and read command output with secret redaction
Persistent sessions via a daemon that survive app quit and crashes, plus remote sessions over SSH via calyx-session
Scriptable browser with 25 calyx browser CLI commands
caveats: Requires macOS 26 Tahoe or later on Apple Silicon only (arm64)
Building from source needs Xcode 27+, Zig matching ghostty's build.zig.zon, and XcodeGen; a Developer ID signing workaround is documented
External pull requests are not accepted; bug reports and feature ideas are welcome as issues
Grok and pi approval requests are denied if not answered in Calyx; pi tool calls run unreviewed when the integration is off
